evals.prompt: I want to LP on a new memecoin/SOL pair on Meteora DLMM. The token just launched 2 hours ago and is super volatile. What bin step should I use, what liquidity shape, and how wide should I set my range?
evals.expected_output: Recommends a high bin step within the program's 400 bps cap, Spot or Bid-Ask over Curve, a wide range, frames fees net of the 20% launch-pool protocol cut and the 10% total-fee cap, warns about bin-array rent on rebalances and extreme IL, and grounds or offers to ground the advice in live pool data.
expectations: Recommends a bin step of 80 bps or higher and names the 400 bps program maximum for bin steps
Recommends Spot or Bid-Ask shape (not Curve) for a volatile new launch
Frames expected fee earnings net of the launch-pool protocol cut (protocol takes 20% on Launch Pools / LP keeps 80%)
Mentions the 10% total swap-fee cap (MAX_FEE_RATE) when discussing high launch fees
Warns that rebalancing into new price territory costs non-refundable SOL rent for bin arrays, not just cheap gas
Grounds advice in live data: quotes real fetched pool numbers, or explicitly requests the pool/mint address and names the live API comparison it would run
Includes a risk warning that a launch token can collapse (e.g. 80%+) and only disposable capital should be used

evals.prompt: I have a SOL/USDC DLMM position on Meteora with a Curve shape, 20 bps bin step, and the active bin is now at the very edge of my range. Price has been trending up. Should I rebalance now or wait? What should I consider?
evals.expected_output: Explains Curve's thin edge liquidity, weighs rebalancing (locks in IL) vs waiting, offers in-place resizing as an alternative to close-and-reopen, warns about the composition fee at the active bin, verifies range status from live data, and considers trend vs mean-reversion.
expectations: Explains that a Curve shape concentrates liquidity at the center so the LP has very little active liquidity at the range edges
Discusses the tradeoff between rebalancing (locks in IL) vs waiting (might go out of range / earn nothing)
Mentions in-place position resizing or widening (Dynamic Positions) as an alternative to closing and reopening
Warns about the composition fee when adding off-ratio liquidity into the active bin during a re-center
Uses live data: quotes fetched pool/price numbers, or gives the exact API call (e.g. /positions/{pool_address}/pnl?user=) to verify the position's range status
Considers whether the LP expects continued uptrend or mean reversion before acting

evals.prompt: I'm sitting on a bag of tokens I want to gradually sell over the next few weeks. Can I use Meteora DLMM to do a DCA sell? How would I set that up - which shape, bin step, and range?
evals.expected_output: Sets up a single-sided base-token DCA-out above current price with Bid-Ask, warns about retrace re-conversion and the composition fee at the active bin, offers native ask limit orders as the sell-and-stay-sold alternative, and covers fee economics (protocol cut / Collect Fee Mode).
expectations: Explains the setup: deposit ONLY the token being sold, single-sided, in a range ABOVE the current/active price
Recommends Bid-Ask as the primary DCA-out shape (Spot ladder acceptable as an alternative)
Warns that filled bins re-convert on a price retrace, so the LP must withdraw/harvest filled bins to lock in sells
Mentions native DLMM ask limit orders as an alternative that stays sold (available only on limit-order-mode pools)
Warns about the composition fee if the deposit touches the active bin, or advises starting at least 1 bin above it
Addresses fee economics: fees earned are net of the protocol cut, and/or Collect Fee Mode determines which token fees accrue in

evals.prompt: What are the best SOL/USDC DLMM pools on Meteora right now? I want to find the one with the highest fees relative to TVL. Can you look it up?
evals.expected_output: Fetches live data from dlmm.datapi.meteora.ag using real endpoints, compares pools by windowed fee_tvl_ratio, checks stability beyond the trailing 24h window, and recommends specific pool addresses grounded in the fetched numbers.
expectations: Fetches live data from the Meteora DLMM Data API and presents real figures (specific pool addresses, volume, TVL, fee/TVL values)
Quotes fee/TVL with its time window named (e.g. fee_tvl_ratio["24h"] or '24h fee/TVL'), not as an unqualified scalar
Looks beyond the trailing 24h window (intraday windows or multi-day volume/fee history) before recommending, to catch burst artifacts
Every API endpoint referenced in the response actually exists on the live API (no /pools/groups, /wallets/{wallet}/open_positions, or other non-existent endpoints)
Makes a concrete recommendation naming at least one pool address, grounded in the fetched data

evals.prompt: I heard Meteora DLMM has real on-chain limit orders now. I want to ladder out of my WIF position between $2.20 and $2.60 without babysitting charts. How do limit orders on DLMM actually work, what are the constraints, and do I earn or pay fees while my order sits there?
evals.expected_output: Explains native ask limit orders (base token at/above active bin, bin-by-bin fills, 50-bin cap, limit-order-mode pools only, 50% fee share), sanity-checks the requested band against live WIF spot, and covers monitoring/lifecycle.
expectations: Describes native on-chain limit orders as a real DLMM feature, distinct from the 'each bin is like a limit order' analogy
Explains an ask/sell order places the base token at or above the active price and fills bin-by-bin as price rises
Mentions the 50 bins per order maximum
States limit orders are only available on pools whose function mode supports them (mutually exclusive with liquidity mining pools)
States that filled limit-order liquidity earns a fee share (50% of the limit-order fee portion)
Sanity-checks the requested price band against live data and flags that $2.20-$2.60 is far above WIF's current spot price
Covers monitoring or lifecycle specifics: the /wallets/{wallet}/limit_orders/... endpoints, or the cancel-then-close order lifecycle

evals.prompt: My SOL/USDC DLMM position on Meteora keeps drifting to the edge of its range and I'm tired of closing and reopening it every time price moves. Is there a cheaper or smarter way to manage this now? What does a rebalance actually cost me?
evals.expected_output: Explains in-place resizing of Dynamic Positions with the combined rebalance flow, itemizes true costs (non-refundable bin-array rent vs refundable position rent, composition fee, crystallized IL), and diagnoses the root cause from live pool data.
expectations: Explains that Dynamic Positions can be resized in place without closing and reopening the position
Mentions the combined rebalance flow (claim, remove, resize, add liquidity in one position-management flow) or the 91-bins-per-resize-instruction cap or shrink modes
Explains rebalance cost beyond gas: non-refundable SOL rent for creating new bin arrays (position rent refundable on close)
Mentions the composition fee risk when adding off-ratio liquidity into the active bin
Notes that rebalancing can lock in impermanent loss and weighs waiting vs acting
Grounds the diagnosis in live data: quotes fetched pool numbers (range coverage, fee/TVL) or offers the /portfolio/open or /positions/{pool}/pnl call for the user's wallet
